message.content:
### Killing Visual Studio Code (`code.exe`) from the Windows command line

> **Tip:**  
> Use `taskkill` with the **image name** (`code.exe`) instead of a PID.  
> This works even if you don’t know the exact process ID or if there are several VS Code windows open.

---

#### 1. Open a Command Prompt (or PowerShell)

```cmd
cmd
```

or

```powershell
powershell
```

---

#### 2. Find the running VS Code processes (optional)

```cmd
tasklist | findstr /i code.exe
```

You’ll see something like:

```
code.exe                 1234 Console                    1     45,678 K
code.exe                 5678 Console                    1     12,345 K
```

The numbers after the name are the **PIDs** (process IDs).

---

#### 3. Kill all VS Code instances

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM code.exe` – target the image name  
* `/F` – force termination (no prompt)

If you want to also terminate any child processes that were spawned by VS Code (e.g., extension workers), add `/T`:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

---

#### 4. Kill a specific instance (by PID)

If you only want to close one window, use the PID you found earlier:

```cmd
taskkill /PID 1234 /F
```

---

#### 5. Using PowerShell (alternative)

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or for a specific PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id 1234 -Force
```

---

### What to Expect

* All VS Code windows will close immediately.  
* Any unsaved work will be lost—make sure you’ve saved before running the command.  
* If you’re running VS Code as a normal user, you usually don’t need admin rights.  
* If you get “Access is denied”, run the command prompt as **Administrator**.

---

### Quick Reference Cheat‑Sheet

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Force‑kill all VS Code processes |
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` | Force‑kill all VS Code processes **and** their child processes |
| `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Force‑kill a single VS Code instance |
| `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of the first command |
| `Stop-Process -Id <pid> -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of the third command |

That’s all you need to shut down VS Code from the command line!
